# git Provider

Manages a git repository from Terraform: the branches you track, and the quilt-style patch stack applied on top of them. Use the [`git_repository`](../data-sources/repository.md) data source to point at a repository that already exists, [`git_branch`](../resources/branch.md) to track a branch and apply patches to it, and [`git_patch`](../data-sources/patch.md) to pull a patch out of a file, an inline diff, a GitHub PR or commit, or a GitLab MR or commit.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    git = {
      source = "UnstoppableMango/git"
    }
  }
}

provider "git" {
  # "go-git" (default) or "exec".
  git_implementation = "go-git"

  # Optional default auth, used by any resource/data source that doesn't
  # set its own auth.token.
  auth = {
    token = "ghp_..."
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `auth` (Attributes) Default credentials for connecting to repositories and hosts, used whenever a resource or data source doesn't set its own `auth.token`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--auth))
- `git_implementation` (String) Which git implementation to use behind the scenes. One of `go-git` or `exec`. Defaults to `go-git`.

<a id="nestedatt--auth"></a>
### Nested Schema for `auth`

Optional:

- `token` (String, Sensitive) Default token for authenticating with a repository host. Any resource can override it.
